service.description: The integrations of the user's stores (or one store): each binding of a registered connector (a SystemMessageRemote with the store and connector, or an EDI partner's connection), with its store, connector, direction, whether its intake is enabled, whether credentials are set (never what they are), its mapping, last success, failures, conflicts and EDI exceptions and a health key (disabled, credentials, failing, conflicts, ok, idle). By connector, enabled (Y or N) and health. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope.
The connectors a store's channel operator may bind: registered (StoreChannelConnector), enabled, implemented by StoreChannels.js and not the EDI administrator's. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE.

One integration: the binding as find#StoreIntegrations shows it, its typed mapping parameters with their values, the registered mapping versions and import formats, and for an EDI partner its rejected and quarantined transactions (documents and interchanges, each with its reason and safe error, never its text). COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope.

Without systemMessageRemoteId, binds a store to a registered connector (productStoreId, connectorId, description, mappingVersion, its typed parameters): a new SystemMessageRemote with its intake stopped and an HMAC signature required until the operator has set its credentials. With one, changes its description, mapping version, typed parameters (customerPartyId: a Customer-role party; salesChannelEnumId) and enabled (Y needs the mapping complete, an authentication method and credentials set: CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED). Never a credential, an endpoint or an authentication method; the store and connector are fixed (STORE_FIXED, CONNECTOR_FIXED); an EDI partner is the EDI administrator's (EDI_MANAGED); expectedLastUpdatedStamp refuses a stale form (STALE_REVISION). The mapping fields are audit-logged. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope.

The messages of the user's stores' integrations (or one, systemMessageRemoteId), newest first: by state (failed, conflict, duplicate, applied, waiting), direction (in, out), parent (a receipt's or a batch's orders) and an external or message ID (term); a page at a time. Each row: ID, kind, direction, external ID, state, attempts, received and processed times, the safe first line of its error, its order, the original of a replay or conflict and whether retry#StoreMessages retries it. Never a message's text. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope.

One message's safe summary (design §9 MessageDetail): its row as find#StoreMessages shows it, its errors' first lines, a channel order's canonical fields (external ID, placed date, lines with product, quantity and price, shipping, tax, note; never the message's text or anything else the channel sent), what its mapping finds when it was not applied, its order (with orderView, whether the user may open it), the original of a replay or conflict, a receipt's or batch's orders, and an EDI receipt's documents. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope.

An operator's retry of failed messages (systemMessageIds) and EDI documents (ediDocumentIds) of one integration, with a reason, each in its own transaction and keeping its identity: a channel order consumed again as the same message (an order already made is never made again), an EDI receipt consumed again from its kept bytes, an EDI document applied or sent again with its controls (X12.js). A conflict is kept as evidence and not retried (CONFLICT_REVIEW), nor a duplicate or an applied one (NOT_RETRYABLE). Keyed by operationKey on PostingOperation: a second submit answers the first result (alreadyApplied). The results name each item. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope; at most 100 at a time. Registered as an operational recovery action (find#MessageRecoveryTargets and recover#StoreMessage below; mr-boss impl-admin P13).

One item of retry#StoreMessages, run in its own transaction and checked again (COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope): a message (systemMessageId) or an EDI document (ediDocumentId) of the integration. ok when it is now applied.

Store channel messages as a registered operational recovery (moqui.server.RecoveryDescriptor rows in data/StoreChannelSetupData.xml; the framework's org.moqui.admin.OperationServices): which of the given system messages are a store integration's, and for each whether retry#StoreMessages would take it now for this caller (retryEligible, with the reason when not), its state and its integration (ownerRef), answered only within the caller's own COMMERCE_VIEW, COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and store scope: a message of a store outside it is answered as held, with no state or detail. Nothing is reconciled or cancelled here and no payload is shown. It changes nothing.

The registered recovery action on one store channel message: a retry is retry#StoreMessages for that message, with the reason and the operation key (a repeat answers the first result), so its identity is kept and an order already made is never made again; anything else is not offered (NOT_OFFERED). COMMERCE_VIEW, COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope, checked by retry#StoreMessages: the registration adds no right.

The StoreChannelOrders type's receive service (receive#IncomingSystemMessage, behind /rest/sm with the remote authenticated by the endpoint; commit#ChannelImport with its batch as parentMessageId). The remote must be a store's binding of a registered intake connector of this type, its intake enabled (an import's batch needs only the binding). The receipt is kept as it came (an unreadable one in error), then each order of it ({orders:[...]}, a list or one order) its own message by the store, remote, kind and external ID with the hash of its canonical content: new, Received (systemMessageIdList, to consume); a matching replay, Consumed as a duplicate answering the original's order; a conflicting one, Rejected and quarantined with the evidence of what differs.

The StoreChannelOrders type's consume service: one received channel order made through create#Order and create#OrderItem (the store's currency, organization and facility, the binding's customer and sales channel, the channel's prices, its shipping and tax as items, promotions and shipping and tax calculation off) and placed (place#Order; approval is the seller's), linked to its message (orderId, OrderSystemMessage). Refused with the first finding's code (ITEM_UNKNOWN, ITEM_UNAVAILABLE, CURRENCY_MISMATCH, LINE_QUANTITY_INVALID, MAPPING_INCOMPLETE, ...). A message whose order was made answers it.
The StoreChannelImport type's receive service: a batch is made only by prepare#ChannelImport, so a post of this type to the message endpoint is refused.

return.message: IMPORT_NOT_REMOTE: a channel import batch is prepared in Commerce, not posted

service.description: ChannelImport's ImportSource (design §9): a file (importFile, or importText with fileName) of a registered format (formatEnumId: SciCsv, one row per order line; SciJson, the API's message) for an integration whose connector imports, read (UTF-8, at most 2 MiB and 500 orders; another format or an unreadable file is refused) and kept as a Staged batch, a SystemMessage of type StoreChannelImport (the same file for the same integration answers the batch already staged). Answers get#ChannelImport's preview. No order is made. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope.

A channel import batch (design §9 ImportPreview and ImportResult): its integration, store, format, file name, digest and state, who committed it, when and why; while staged, each order's predicted outcome (a new order, a duplicate of one received before or earlier in the file, a conflict and what differs, or the finding it will fail with); once committed, each order's message with its outcome, order and safe error, and whether it is retried. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope. Admin §11 registers ChannelImport as an import target when it is built (impl-commerce §7).

Internal, for commit#ChannelImport, in a transaction of its own: the batch locked and, while it is still staged, marked committing (claimed true); a batch another commit claimed first answers claimed false. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope.

ChannelImport's ImportCommit: the staged batch as previewed (digest; another is BATCH_CHANGED) committed with a reason, its orders received through the API's connector path (receive#ChannelOrders with the batch as parent: deduplicated, replays answered, conflicts quarantined) and each consumed in its own transaction, a failing order not stopping the others; the batch Consumed and the commit recorded (PostingOperation ChannelImport:{batch}, its reason and counts). Committing again answers the outcome (alreadyApplied); a commit that fails before its orders are kept leaves the batch staged, and committing it again keeps no order twice. COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope.

The feeds of the user's stores (Feeds; FeedFind's store, site, format and state: current by default, ended or all), each with its format, destination, public path, schedule, active build, latest and last complete build (rows, skips, errors, failure) and revision.
One feed of the user's stores (FeedDetail's FeedConfig) with its newest builds (FeedBuilds; limit, 20 by default, at most 50), never an artifact. Another store's is RECORD_UNAVAILABLE.

A new feed of a store (NewFeed), a change to one at its revision (FeedConfig: STALE_REVISION naming the current one) or one ended (ended Y). Only a registered format (FORMAT_UNREGISTERED) and destination (DESTINATION_UNREGISTERED); the site's Shop must sell from the store (SITE_INVALID); the locale and currency are the store's (VALUE_INVALID); the key is unique among the site's current feeds (FEED_KEY_TAKEN). A change of site, key, format or category clears the active build.

Build a feed now (FeedPreview's Build), in its own transaction (run#StoreFeedBuild): a complete build of Shop's public projection at the site's generation, with its rows, skips (each product and why) and errors; a fatal problem (SITE_UNAVAILABLE, HOST_REQUIRED) is recorded as a failed build and the active build is left as it was. The build is not published.

One build of a feed in the caller's transaction (build#StoreFeed's and the feed job's step; a signed-in caller is checked as build#StoreFeed checks), published when publish is Y and it has no errors. A fatal problem is thrown for the caller to record.

A build (FeedBuilds, FeedPreview, PublishFeed): its dates, generation, rows, skips with product names, errors, artifact digest and size, the sample rows of the public projection, and whether it can be published now (complete, of the feed's format, not active, every product still public: withdrawn names the ones that are not); with withArtifact Y its artifact (the operator's download).

Make a complete build the feed's active one (PublishFeed), at the feed's revision (STALE_REVISION) with an operation key (PostingOperation StoreFeedPublish: a retry answers the first result). Refuses a failed build (BUILD_INCOMPLETE), one of another format (BUILD_OUTDATED) and one with a product withdrawn since it was built (BUILD_STALE).

Channel health (design-commerce §3 ChannelHealth) of the user's stores (one, several or all) for a period (fromDate, thruDate; the last 30 days by default, at most two years, PERIOD_INVALID): by store, remote and message type the messages received (processed, failed, retried, last success; never a payload, address or credential), and each current feed's last complete build with its rows and skips, its failed builds in the period, the latest failure and whether serving is blocked by a withdrawal; totals (attention: message errors and failing feeds).

The run_StoreFeeds job: each current feed on an hourly or daily schedule whose interval has passed, built in its own transaction (run#StoreFeedBuild) and published when complete with no errors; a failure is recorded as a failed build of that feed and the others go on. The job holds no transaction of its own, so each feed's failure record and schedule stamp commit as they are written and no feed row stays locked while the others build.

getShopFeed: the active build of a current feed of the site's Shop by input.feedKey and input.extension (the format's), served only while every product in it is public at the site's current generation; anything else is NotFound (FEED_UNAVAILABLE). result.content, contentType, digest, generation, builtGeneration, builtDate.

The channel import batches of the stores the caller operates (COMMERCE_VIEW, COMMERCE_CHANNEL_OPERATE and the store scope, as get#ChannelImport), newest first, as summaries: the file's name and store, the store's organization, staged, committing or committed, how many orders a commit took, who committed it, and the parameters that open the batch in ChannelImport. None otherwise.
